ideas.title: A hand mirror, and friends who chase the sun spot
ideas.goal: The player as Lumi tilts a little mirror (mouse or Q/E) and throws a bright spot of sunlight anywhere on the island; friends chase it like cats chase a laser, pounce on it, bump into each other, and a sleeping friend wakes when it lands on its face. Fun: a toy that turns the whole island into a game of tag you steer with light, and you get good at leading them into the pond.
ideas.idea: The spot is real: the sun direction reflected off the mirror's normal, traced against the island (Raycore BVH) to where it lands; its size grows with distance (the sun's 0.5 degree disc), its brightness falls on a slope. Friends see it if it is in their field of view and chase with a pounce when close. In the path tracer the mirror is a Hikari Conductor and the spot is real reflected light, with a caustic glint on the leaves.
ideas.form: A plugin with a key while jumped in, a friend behaviour, and a traced short of three friends tumbling after the spot down to the beach.

ideas.title: Dominoes across the island
ideas.goal: Walking as Lumi, the player lays a domino behind every step (D held down), along paths, round trees, up the steps of the gallery; then tips the first and watches the run go, splitting at forks and stopping where a gap is too wide. Fun: building something long with your own hands and the big release when it all falls, and getting good at curves and gaps.
ideas.idea: Each domino is a real rigid box (PrintSim affine bodies with IPC contact on Mantle) standing on the terrain; the wave speed comes out of the physics (spacing, height, slope), so a run downhill speeds up and a run uphill can stall. Friends lay their own short runs and cheer when theirs falls.
ideas.form: A plugin on PrintSim's rigid bodies, a key for laying and tipping, and a traced short following the falling front across the meadow.

ideas.title: The owl that hunts by ear
ideas.goal: At night the player as a small friend sneaks from the hedge to the berry bush past an owl in the big tree. Every step makes a sound: loud on gravel and dry leaves, soft on moss and grass, louder when you run. If the owl hears you, its head turns, then it glides down. Fun: a stealth game where your ears and feet matter, with real risk and a real escape (freeze and it loses you).
ideas.idea: Footstep loudness from the ground material and speed; the sound goes out through my acoustic ray tracer (physics/echo.jl) and the owl hears what really reaches its two ears (time and level difference, like a barn owl), with trees and the cottage in the way blocking it. It turns its head toward where the arrivals come from, so a sound bounced off the cottage wall fools it.
ideas.form: A mini game (Owl walk) with a new owl creature from a generated asset, a listening system, and a traced night short of a near miss.

ideas.title: Glass blowing at the furnace
ideas.goal: At a furnace by the workshop the player gathers a glowing blob on a pipe, blows (hold Space) and turns it (A/D), lets it sag or swings it long, and shapes a vase, a bulb or a wobbly mistake; it cools from orange to clear and goes on a shelf where the sun shines through it. Fun: shaping a soft hot thing by feel, every piece different, and a shelf of your own glass.
ideas.idea: The glass is a viscous shell of revolution: a 1D profile of rings with thickness, temperature and viscosity that rises steeply as it cools; inner pressure inflates it, gravity sags it, spinning holds it round. It glows as a blackbody while hot and is a Hikari dielectric once cool, so the shelf throws coloured caustics.
ideas.form: A workshop station plugin with its own small solver, and a traced still of the shelf in morning light.

ideas.title: Spinning tops on the cairn table
ideas.goal: The player and the friends spin tops on the flat stone; the player picks a top, winds it with a pull (hold and release), and launches it into the bowl; tops precess, clash, wobble, and the last one spinning wins. Fun: a tiny battle game you get good at (angle and pull strength) with a winner shouting.
ideas.idea: Each top is a real rigid body with Euler's equations: spin, gravity torque, precession and nutation, friction at the tip that makes it rise (the sleeping top), and collisions that kick spin out of the loser. Friends play rounds by themselves and rematch.
ideas.form: A mini game with its own rigid body integrator (or PrintSim affine bodies), generated wooden tops, and a traced slow-motion clash.

ideas.title: The morning paper
ideas.goal: Every island morning a printed paper flaps down onto the cottage step; its front page is what really happened yesterday ("Gloop skips nine!", "Paint war at the pond", "Lumi thrown into orbit") with a photo from the night. The player can try to make tomorrow's headline by doing something big, and the friends read it and talk about it all day. Fun: your play becomes news that the island remembers.
ideas.idea: The headlines come from the event log, ranked by how rare and how big each event was; the photo is a still the game takes at that moment. The paper is a real sheet (PrintSim cloth) that blows across the meadow if nobody picks it up.
ideas.form: A plugin for the paper and the friends' reactions, a page in the browser for the front page, and a traced short of the paper blowing across the meadow at dawn.

ideas.title: Hide and seek in the dark, by clapping
ideas.goal: Project island-echo: on a dark night four friends hide; the player as Lumi claps (N) and sees, for a moment, the island as the sound found it, and a hidden friend lights up as a shape where the echo hits it. Find them all before dawn; each clap also tells the friends where you are, so they creep away.
ideas.idea: The echo rays hit the friends' bodies too (their meshes in the BVH), so a friend behind a bush shows only the part the sound reaches; friends hear the clap with the real delay and move after it.
ideas.form: A mini game on top of the clap, and a traced night short of a find.

ideas.title: Reed duel at the pond
ideas.goal: Two friends, or the player against a friend, fence with long pond reeds; a parry at the right moment bends the other reed away and opens a poke; a hard clash knocks the reed out of a hand into the water. Fun: a timing duel with a read on your opponent, short rounds, and a splash for the loser.
ideas.idea: Each reed is a real elastic rod (a chain of segments with bending stiffness) that swings with inertia and bends on contact; the grip is a spring that lets go above a force. Friends duel by themselves with personalities (cautious, wild).
ideas.form: A mini game with a rod solver, and a traced short of a knock-out into the pond.

ideas.title: The tide
ideas.goal: The sea rises and falls twice an island day. At low tide the beach is wide and rock pools appear with crabs, shells and stranded fish the player can carry back; at high tide the sea climbs the beach, takes whatever was left there, and the pier stands in water. Fun: a rhythm to the island and a reason to go to the shore at the right time.
ideas.idea: The water level follows the moon (two highs a day, bigger at full moon); the terrain decides where pools are left when it drops. Things left on the beach float off at high tide and wash up elsewhere.
ideas.form: An engine change to the sea level plus a plugin for the pools and drifting things, and a traced timelapse of a tide coming in.

ideas.title: Paper planes
ideas.goal: Project paper-letters: the player folds a paper plane (a key) and throws it; it glides, stalls, loops or dives depending on the throw, and the friends fold their own and hold a distance contest from the lookout. Fun: a skill throw you get better at, and a contest with the island.
ideas.idea: The plane is a real folded sheet (PrintSim) with my air drag and a pitching moment, so it glides for real; a bent wingtip makes it turn.
ideas.form: A plugin using PrintSim on Mantle, and a traced short of a long glide from the lookout.
